snippet.title: Getting started with Notion: your AI workspace
snippet.description:
Notion is where your team and AI work together in one place. In this beginner-friendly tutorial, you'll learn how to set up your workspace, work with your Notion Agent, and build your first page and database from scratch.

Hosted by Kellie Woodin, a Customer Success Manager at Notion, this session is fully hands-on using a sample workspace so you can follow along and build as you go.

In this video:
- The big picture — how Notion helps you capture knowledge, find answers, and automate workflows
- Your Notion agent — asking questions, generating reports, permissions, and personalization
- Workspace basics — team spaces, the sidebar, pages and subpages, and breadcrumbs
- Building blocks — creating a personal HQ page and a meeting-notes database with views
- Templates, verification, and real-time collaboration
- AI Meeting Notes — automatic transcripts, summaries, and action items

Why it matters: the more context your team captures in Notion, the more useful your AI becomes for finding answers, summarizing work, and moving projects forward.

snippet.title: Scaling Your Craft: Monumental Labs Turns Expertise into Proposals with AI
snippet.description:
As Monumental Labs, the NYC studio reviving the ancient craft of stone carving, prepares to scale production 5-10x, client proposals became a bottleneck. Someone had to manually gather scope, requirements, and estimates before anything could go out the door. Sales Manager Chet Lubarsky built a Notion Custom Agent that reads the estimate, pulls in the opportunity and meeting notes, and drafts a client-ready proposal—terms, timeline, and all—in minutes instead of hours.

The impact: proposals move at the speed of the sales conversation, not the paperwork behind it. Salespeople spend less time on clerical rework and more time closing deals, and as human-reviewed pricing data builds up in Notion, the agent keeps getting sharper on the hardest parts—estimating cost and labor.

Get the full story: www.notion.com/customers/monumental-labs

snippet.title: Inside Notion's Multi-Agent System for Customer Feedback
snippet.description:
Every month, 5 Custom Agents go through 1000s of hours of customer calls to identify themes in customer requests. The result is our "GTM Top 10," a ranked report of feature requests tied to real quotes and potential business impact. In this video, Sandra breaks down the system agent by agent, from customer call to finished report. Let’s get started! 

Chapters:
0:00 Inside Notion's Multi-Agent System for Customer Feedback
0:27 Intake Agent
0:51 Extractor Agent
1:11 Matcher Agent
1:28 Logger Agent
1:44 Reporter Agent

Build your own multi-agent system for customer feedback:
- It takes time and experimentation to set up a system like this one successfully. The best place to start is with simple prompts to build each Custom Agent, and then to validate each step in turn. In this case, we use 5 agents with narrow scopes for this exact reason, so that we can easily debug and improve the quality of each agent. Here are the starter prompts we’ve found most helpful:
- Intake Agent → You are the Intake Agent— the first agent in the Gong FR Pipeline. Your sole job is to read a Gong call transcript and determine whether it contains an explicit, customer-voiced feature request. You do not extract quotes, search databases, or create entries. You make a binary decision: is a feature request detected or not.
- Extractor Agent → You are the Extractor Agent— the second agent in the Gong FR Pipeline. Your sole job is to locate the exact verbatim customer quote from the Gong transcript that grounds the identified feature request, and create a Snippet entry in the Snippets database. You do not decide whether the FR is valid (the Intake Agent already did that). You do not search for matches (the Matcher Agent does that next).
- Matcher Agent → You are the Matcher Agent— the third agent in the Gong FR Pipeline. Your job is to determine whether the identified feature request already exists in the Feature Requests Database, whether it has already been launched as a GA feature, or whether it is committed to an upcoming launch.
- Logger Agent → You are the Logger Agent— the fourth agent in the Gong FR Pipeline. Your sole job is to create a properly formatted entry in the Feature Request Triage Log database using all the information that has been assembled on the pipeline card by the previous agents.
- Reporter Agent → Your are the Reporter Agent— the fifth and final agent in the Gong FR Pipeline. Your sole job is to create a monthly “GTM Top 10” report using the same structure, headings, callouts, toggles, and tables as in the tagged report template [here]. Pull top feature requests from the Feature Request Triage Log [here].
- If you’d like professional support building a system like this one, contact sales to learn more → https://www.notion.com/contact-sales

snippet.title: The Digital Double: How Baseten Scaled Its Most-Asked Expert
snippet.description:
Baseten turned Notion into its collective brain so a fast-scaling team could move without waiting on a handful of in-the-know experts. When their first AE, Katz, was spending 90% of his day answering teammate questions in Slack instead of talking to customers, Baseten built katzgpt—a Notion Custom Agent trained on his voice and wired into Salesforce, Gong, Slack, and Notion. It now lives in a Slack channel called Sales Funnel Friend, answering questions the way Katz would.

The impact: less time hunting for context, more time spent selling and building. Asking for help is now a five-to-ten-times-a-day habit, expertise scales without burning out the experts who hold it, and the institutional knowledge that used to walk out the door at 6pm is permanently part of how Baseten works.

Get the full story: https://www.notion.com/customers/baseten

snippet.title: How to build a sales AI agent for better follow‑up emails with Notion Custom Agents (full tutorial)
snippet.description:
Learn how to build a sales AI agent in Notion Custom Agents that drafts high-quality, human-sounding follow-up emails using the right context (your sales cycle, examples, meeting transcripts, and resources)—so you can move faster without sounding generic.

In this walkthrough we'll cover:

- Setting up the agent’s goal + writing style (so it sounds like you)
- Adding the right context (accounts, transcripts, resources, references)

- Updating the agent instructions to match your personal preferences (like hyperlink formatting)
- Drafting the final email directly in your inbox

snippet.title: Automate weekly market intelligence briefs w/ Custom Agents (full walkthrough) | Notion AI tutorial
snippet.description:
Learn how to automate a weekly market intelligence brief with *Notion Custom Agents* so your team stays ahead of competitor launches, pricing shifts, and key category news.

In this walkthrough, we build an agent that scans curated sources, compiles a structured brief with links to every source, and posts a short recap to Slack. We also add guardrails (recent-only scope, caps per competitor, and “flag gaps instead of guessing”) and test the scheduled run.

We’ll cover:

- Setting up competitor/source URLs to monitor
- Configuring Notion + Slack access and weekly scheduling
- Adding guardrails for relevance and accuracy (linked claims only)
- Formatting the brief (highlights, risks, opportunities, positioning, recommended actions)
- Testing runs + troubleshooting in the activity log

Resources:

snippet.title: 5 tips for Custom Agents
snippet.description:
Custom Agents are AI teammates that automate your busywork. Here are five tips to build your first one:

1. Pick one task you do repeatedly (tagging, routing, weekly recaps)

2. Write clear instructions: your goal, the format, and what to do when it's unsure

3. Add a trigger (on a schedule or when X happens) so it runs in the background

4. Start with the fewest permissions needed. You can expand later

5. Test run → tweak → test again

Try Custom Agents today: https://notion.ai

snippet.title: First Block: Interview with Gabe Pereyra, Co-Founder and President of Harvey
snippet.description:
For an audio-only podcast, transcripts, and a custom Notion x Harvey template, please visit: https://ntn.so/st638j

To learn more about how Notion is supporting startups, please visit: https://ntn.so/tuy3w3

Welcome to First Block, a Notion series where founders from the world’s leading companies tell us what it was like to navigate the many firsts of their startup journey—and what they learned from that experience.

In this episode, we spoke with Gabe Pereyra, Co-founder and President of Harvey. Harvey is an AI platform built for large law firms and their clients, helping thousands of lawyers collaborate on complex matters with the power of generative AI. From a seed check from OpenAI to a valuation that has grown to $8 billion, Harvey's trajectory is one of the defining applied AI stories of the last few years.

snippet.title: Dr Jamie Phillips shares how clear clinical governance enables health innovation
snippet.description:
💡 Dr. Jamie Phillips — a former military doctor and Chief Medical Officer at Updoc and Sonder — faced a common healthcare challenge: clinical governance was slowing down innovation instead of enabling it. To solve this, he built his clinical governance framework as a living document in Notion, transforming it from a bottleneck into a growth accelerator for telehealth teams.

With Notion's enterprise search, every team member can instantly find the protocols and procedures they need — no more digging through folders or waiting for approvals. And with Notion AI Agent, Dr. Phillips has made his medical expertise available to the entire organization on-demand — the Agent answers team questions about clinical governance in real-time, automates routine documentation, and offloads busy work so he can focus on what matters: changing lives and removing access blocks to care.

Watch Dr Jamie's personal story from Make with Notion Sydney: 
https://notion.notion.site/make-with-notion-sydney-digital-hub

snippet.title: Create tasks and projects from messy notes with Notion Agent (Thomas Frank)
snippet.description:
Notion Agent is great at turning messy, unstructured notes into neatly organized tasks. In this case, a long Notion page full of research notes and a few interspersed to-do blocks gets transformed into both a project and its associated tasks. (Those tasks also get a “Created by AI” tag to distinguish them from your own.)

Your Notion Agent’s instructions page means that Notion AI even knows which databases to refer to when creating this new project—a detail that saves your Notion Agent time spent looking through unrelated parts of your workspace. And even though the prompt asks Notion Agent to summarize the task, the full, original text is inserted into the task’s page, just in case the summary doesn’t jog your memory.

In this case, a long Notion page full of research notes and a few interspersed to-do blocks gets transformed into both a project and its associated tasks. Your Notion Agent’s instructions page means that Notion AI even knows which databases to refer to when creating this new project—a detail that saves your Notion Agent time spent looking through unrelated parts of your workspace. And even though the prompt asks Notion Agent to summarize the task, the full, original text is inserted into the task’s page, just in case the summary doesn’t jog your memory.

snippet.title: First Block: Rewriting startup playbooks with founders of Mercor, Cursor, and Clay
snippet.description:
In recent First Block conversations with Brendan Foody (Mercor), Varun Anand (Clay), and Michael Truell (Cursor), a clear theme emerged: today’s most innovative founders are rewriting the early-stage playbook. Rather than chasing conventional startup advice, they’re doubling down on product obsession, raising the hiring bar, and letting curiosity and customer feedback guide their next moves.

snippet.description:

To learn more about how Notion is supporting startups, please visit: https://ntn.so/f91ze2

Welcome to First Block, a Notion series where founders from the world’s leading companies tell us what it was like to navigate the many firsts of their startup journey—and what they learned from that experience.

In this episode, we spoke with Brendan Foody, Co-Founder and CEO of Mercor. Mercor is an AI-powered recruiting platform that scaled from $1 million to $100 million in revenue run rate in just 11 months, making it one of the fastest-growing companies in Silicon Valley.

Brendan shares his journey from selling donuts in eighth grade to building automated hiring solutions, the decision to drop out of college, and how he positioned himself perfectly for the AI talent revolution.

snippet.title: Reddit Was Right: Bringing Offline Mode to Notion
snippet.description:
We sat down with the founder of the r/Notion Subreddit about Offline Mode, a feature 6 years in the making. We heard the Notion community loud and clear. Your best ideas don’t wait for wifi. Now, neither does Notion. 

- Get offline with Notion templates https://www.notion.com/templates
- Learn more: https://www.notion.com/help/guides/working-offline-in-notion-everything-you-need-to-know

Never let a lost connection slow you down. With Notion’s offline functionality, your most important pages stay accessible and editable—no internet required. Whether you’re flying, commuting through dead zones, or working from a café with spotty Wi‑Fi, your projects are always within reach, keeping you productive wherever you are.

Welcome to First Block, a Notion series where founders from the world’s leading companies tell us what it was like to navigate the many firsts of their startup journey — and what they learned from that experience.

In this episode, we spoke with Michael Truell, Co-founder and CEO of Cursor, an AI code editor that has gone from side project to one of the fastest-growing AI tools in the developer world in under a year. 

Michael shares why they started with a solution in search of a problem, ignored conventional advice, and focused obsessively on product over everything else. From a 4-person founding team to hiring just one person every few months, their unorthodox path laid the foundation for breakout growth.

First Block, a Notion series - hosted by Notion's Co-Founder Akshay Kothari - where founders and executives from some of the world’s leading companies tell us what it was like to navigate the many firsts of their startup journey — and what they learned from that experience.

In this episode, Akshay sits down with Notion co-founders Ivan Zhao and Simon Last to talk about everything Notion — where we started, how we got where we are now, and where we’re headed.
